analysis: The code snippet calls the `get` method on `cells` (a List of AbstractMap) and on `descriptor.getFields()` (a List of FieldDescriptor). Both are list `get(int)` calls matching the documented API, which throws IndexOutOfBoundsException if index < 0 or index >= size(). The loop index `i` runs from 0 to `cellsToProcess - 1`. The value of `cellsToProcess` is set to either `cells.size()` (when cells.size() <= descriptor.getFields().size()) or `descriptor.getFields().size()` (when cells.size() > descriptor.getFields().size() and ignoreUnknownValues is true). In both cases, `i < cellsToProcess <= cells.size()` and `i < cellsToProcess <= descriptor.getFields().size()`, so `i` is always within bounds of both lists. If cells.size() > descriptor.getFields().size() and ignoreUnknownValues is false, an exception is thrown before the loop, so `get` is not called. Therefore, the condition for IndexOutOfBoundsException is never satisfied.
answer: The only declared exception is IndexOutOfBoundsException, and its throwing condition is fully avoided by the bounds checks in the loop logic.
